Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Cross-border payments are partially functional in Malawi. Malawi is a member of SADC TCIB (Transactions Cleared on an Immediate Basis), live since 2021; in December 2024, Malawi banks settled 925 SADC-RTGS transactions worth ZAR 239M. The COMESA Digital Retail Payments Platform (DRPP) began user trials between Malawi and Zambia in October 2025, with TNM Mpamba, FDH Bank, and Finca Malawi as early adopters. NatSwitch planned SADC TCIB integration by December 2024. Cross-border functionality exists via SADC-RTGS and nascent COMESA DRPP trials, but full seamless cross-border retail payments are not yet universally operational. Informal cross-border transfers are also common.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: Government-to-person (G2P) payments via digital channels are in active use in Malawi. The Social Cash Transfer Programme (SCTP), which supports over 300,000 households (1.3 million individuals), began transitioning from manual cash to e-payments in 2022, using TNM Mpamba and Airtel Money. As of mid-2024 (IDinsight report), e-payment rollout has occurred in 10+ districts, with full nationwide rollout planned. The GoM committed to digitising all 28 districts by end of 2023. Salary payments to civil servants and NGO/donor cash disbursements also use mobile money. Airtel Money distributed $3.5M USD for NGO partners in early programs. G2P is actively used though not yet fully universal.
